L278@P5: d The incidence of neurotoxicity is dose dependent.
L279@P5: e Manifestations include partial or total deafness, which may be temporary or permanent, and   difficulties with balance,

L285@P6: Reporting of suspected adverse reactions
L286@P6: Reporting suspected adverse reactions after authorisation of the medicinal product is important. It allows continued
L287@P6: monitoring of the benefit/risk balance of the medicinal product. Healthcare professionals are asked to report any suspected
L288@P6: adverse reactions via HPRA Pharmacovigilance.
L289@P6: Website: www.hpra.ie
L290@P6: 4.9 Overdose
L291@P6: Side effects following the use of vinblastine are dose related. Therefore, following administration of more than the
L292@P6: recommended dose, patients can be expected to experience these effects in an exaggerated fashion. Any dose that results in
L293@P6: elimination of platelets and neutrophils from blood and marrow and their precursors from marrow is life-threatening.
L294@P6: The major effect of excessive doses of vinblastine will be on granulocytopoeisis, and this may be life-threatening.
L295@P6: Overdoses occurring during prolonged, consecutive day infusions may be more toxic than the same total dose given by rapid
L296@P6: intravenous administration.
L297@P6: In addition, neurotoxicity similar to that seen with vincristine sulphate may be observed.
L298@P6: Treatment: Supportive care should include:
L299@P6: (1) prevention of the side effects that result from the syndrome of inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone. This
L300@P6: includes restriction of fluid intake and perhaps the use of a diuretic acting on the loop of Henle and distal tubule function;
L301@P6: (2) administration of an anticonvulsant;
L302@P6: (3) prevention and treatment of ileus;
L303@P6: (4) monitoring the patient's cardiovascular system; and
L304@P6: (5) daily blood counts for guidance in transfusion requirement and assessing therisk of infection.
L305@P6: There is no specific antidote. The use of folinic acid in addition to the other supportive measures recommended may be
L306@P6: considered, although, unlike vincristine sulfate, studies have not been conducted to confirm its protective action.
L307@P6: There is no information regarding the effectiveness of dialysis nor of cholestyramine for the treatment of overdose.
L308@P6: Vinblastine Sulfate in the dry state is irregularly and unpredictably absorbed from the gastro- intestinal tract following oral
L309@P6: administration. Absorption of the solution has not been studied. If Vinblastine Sulfate is swallowed, activated charcoal in a
L310@P6: water slurry may be given by mouth along with a cathartic. The use of cholestyramine in this situation has not been reported.
L311@P6: 5 PHARMACOLOGICAL PROPERTIES
L312@P6: 5.1 Pharmacodynamic properties
L313@P6: Pharmacotherapeutic group: Vinca alkaloids and analogues, ATC code: L01CA01
L314@P6: Vinblastine Sulfate is a cytotoxic drug that arrests cell growth at the metaphase. Its actions are more pronounced on the rapidly
L315@P6: dividing cell than on the normal cell. It appears to act, like Vincristine, by binding to the microtubular proteins of the mitotic
L316@P6: spindle, preventing polymerisation.

L273@P6: If risk factors such as renal function disorders, including mild renal impairment, are present, combined administration with
L274@P6: NSAIDs is not recommended. Dehydration may also intensify the toxicity of methotrexate.
L275@P6: Concomitant use of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) and high dose methotrexate should be avoided, especially in patients with
L276@P6: renal impairment.
L277@P6:  Respiratory system: Acute or chronic interstitial pneumonitis, often associated with blood eosinophilia may occur
L278@P6: and deaths have been reported. Symptoms typically include dyspnoea, cough (especially a dry non-productive
L279@P6: cough), thoracic pain and fever for which patients should be monitored at each follow-up visit. Patients should be
L280@P6: informed of the risk of pneumonitis and advised to contact their doctor immediately should they develop
L281@P6: persistent cough or dyspnoea.
L282@P6: In addition, pulmonary alveolar haemorrhage has been reported with methotrexate used in rheumatologic and related
L283@P6: indications. This event may also be associated with vasculitis and other comorbidities. Prompt investigations should be
L284@P6: considered when pulmonary alveolar haemorrhage is suspected to confirm the diagnosis.
L285@P6: Methotrexate should be withdrawn from patients with pulmonary symptoms and a thorough investigation (including chest
L286@P6: x-ray) should be made to exclude infection. If methotrexate induced lung disease is suspected treatment with corticosteroids
L287@P6: should be initiated and treatment with methotrexate should not be restarted.
L288@P6: Pulmonary symptoms require a quick diagnosis and discontinuation of methotrexate therapy. Pulmonary toxicity and
L289@P6: pulmonary lesions (see section 4.8) can occur acutely at any time and at all dosages during therapy.
L290@P6:  Methotrexate may, due to its effect on the immune system, impair the response to vaccination and interfere with
L291@P6: the results of immunological tests. Particular caution is also needed in the presence of inactive, chronic infections
L292@P6: (e.g. herpes zoster, tuberculosis, hepatitis B or C) due to possible activation. Concurrent vaccination using live
L293@P6: vaccines should not be carried out.
L294@P6:  Malignant lymphomas may occur in patients receiving low dose methotrexate, in which case therapy must be
L295@P6: discontinued. Failure of the lymphoma to show signs of spontaneous regression requires the initiation of cytotoxic
L296@P6: therapy.
L297@P6:  Pleural effusions and ascites should be drained prior to initiation of methotrexate treatment (see section 4.2).
L298@P6:  Diarrhoea and ulcerative stomatitis can be toxic effects and require interruption of therapy, otherwise
L299@P6: haemorrhagic enteritis and death from intestinal perforation may occur.
L300@P6:  Vitamin preparations or other products containing folic acid, folinic acid or their derivatives may decrease the
L301@P6: effectiveness of methotrexate.
L302@P6:  Photosensitivity: Photosensitivity manifested by an exaggerated sunburn reaction has been observed in some
L303@P6: individuals taking methotrexate (see section 4.8). Exposure to intense sunlight or UV rays should be avoided unless
L304@P6: medically indicated. Patients should use adequate sun-protection to protect themselves from intense sunlight.
L305@P6:  Skin toxicity: Epidermal necrosis, mostly accompanied by leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and mucosal lesions, has
L306@P6: been reported with methotrexate treatment (see section 4.8). This cutaneous reaction may clinically mimic
L307@P6: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN). Patients should be advised of the signs and
L308@P6: symptoms of the severe cutaneous adverse reactions and should seek medical advice from their physician

L151@P4: Anti-emetic prophylaxis with corticosteroids such as dexamethasone must be administered to all
L152@P4: patients (see section 4.2).
L153@P4: Rhabdomyolysis and severe CPK elevations (> 5 x ULN)
L154@P4: Trabectedin must not be used in patients with CPK > 2.5 x ULN (see section 4.2). Rhabdomyolysis
L155@P4-5: has been uncommonly reported, usually in association with myelotoxicity, severe liver function test 6
L156@P5: abnormalities and/or renal or multiorgan failure. Therefore, CPK should be closely monitored
L157@P5: whenever a patient may be experiencing any of these toxicities or muscle weakness or muscle pain. If
L158@P5: rhabdomyolysis occurs, supportive measures such as parenteral hydration, urine alkalinisation and
L159@P5: dialysis should be promptly established, as indicated. Treatment with Yondelis should be discontinued
L160@P5: until the patient fully recovers.
L161@P5: Caution should be taken if medicinal products associated with rhabdomyolysis (e.g. statins), are
L162@P5: administered concomitantly with trabectedin, since the risk of rhabdomyolysis may be increased
L163@P5: Liver Function Test (LFT) abnormalities
L164@P5: Reversible acute increases in aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT)
L165@P5: have been reported in most patients. Yondelis must not be used in patients with elevated bilirubin.
L166@P5: Patients with increases in AST, ALT and alkaline phosphatase between cycles may necessitate dose
L167@P5: adjustments (see section 4.2).
L168@P5: Injection site reactions
L169@P5: The use of central venous access is strongly recommended (see section 4.2). Patients may develop a
L170@P5: potentially severe injection site reaction when trabectedin is administered through a peripheral venous
L171@P5: line.
L172@P5: Trabectedin extravasation may cause tissue necrosis requiring debridement. There is no specific
L173@P5: antidote for extravasation of trabectedin. Extravasation should be managed by local standard practice.
L174@P5: Allergic Reactions
L175@P5: During postmarketing experience, hypersensitivity reactions with very rare occurrence of fatal
L176@P5: outcome, have been reported in association with trabectedin administration either alone or in
L177@P5: combination with PLD (see sections 4.3 and 4.8).
L178@P5: Cardiac Dysfunction
L179@P5: Patients should be monitored for cardiac-related adverse events or myocardial dysfunction.
L180@P5: A thorough cardiac assessment including determination of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) by
L181@P5: echocardiogram or multigated acquisition scan (MUGA) should be conducted before initiation of
L182@P5: trabectedin and at 2 to 3-month intervals thereafter until trabectedin is discontinued.
L183@P5: Patients with LVEF less than the lower limit of normal (LVEF < LLN), prior cumulative anthracycline
L184@P5: dose of >300mg/m2
L185@P5: , aged > 65 years, or a history of cardiovascular disease (especially in those with
L186@P5: cardiac medication) may be at increased risk of cardiac dysfunction at treatment with trabectedin as
L187@P5: monotherapy or in combination with doxorubicin.
L188@P5: For patients with Grade 3 or 4 cardiac adverse events indicative of cardiomyopathy or for patients with
L189@P5: a LVEF that decreases below the LLN (assessed as either an absolute decrease of LVEF of ≥15% or
L190@P5: <LLN with an absolute decrease of ≥5%), trabectedin should be discontinued.
